text:
Mason Lohrei has 3 goals in 18 games, more than his chances would suggest (1.38 expected goals), and the Bruins have scored about 4.6 more goals than they deserve with him on the ice. Enjoy it. Both numbers point the same way: this start is running a little lucky.

The underlying worry is defense. Boston takes 48% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with Lohrei on the ice at five on five and is more than six points better without him. Evolving-Hockey's read on last season was harsher: opponents got more chances with him out there than with almost any other defenseman (bottom 4%). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking does credit him with clean exits (56% with possession), which is why he keeps his spot.

He's also a name in trade talk: a Yahoo Sports pitch had Detroit sending Simon Edvinsson to Boston for a package led by Lohrei. That's a pitch, not a report. He's 25, an Ohio State product from Baton Rouge, and he's playing almost 18 minutes a night on a team that's 13-4-1. We project about 29 points. Watch his pair's shot share as the goals cool.
headline: Lohrei's goals hide the questions
